content.title: About
content.content: A butterscotch or caramel topping is a thick sweet sauce made from sugar, butter, cream and flavorings. It is used to drizzle over ice cream, desserts, pancakes, waffles and drinks, giving them a rich buttery‑caramel taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The term “butterscotch” comes from butter and scotch, though the product has no connection to Scotland.
Caramel toppings often contain sea salt, which enhances sweetness through flavor contrast.
In the United States the topping is frequently served as a soft‑serve sauce that stays pourable at low temperatures.
Traditional recipes caramelize sugar before adding butter and cream to achieve a smooth texture.
Vegan versions exist, replacing dairy butter and cream with plant‑based alternatives.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Sugar and fats provide quick calories, which can be useful during high energy demand.

items.title: Contains vitamin A
items.content: Butter contributes a modest amount of vitamin A, important for vision and immunity.

items.title: Mood enhancer
items.content: Sweet taste stimulates serotonin production, helping improve mood.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive consumption may raise blood glucose levels and contribute to tooth decay.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Large amounts of butter increase saturated fat intake, which can affect cardiovascular health.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: People with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy should choose vegan alternatives.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drizzle over ice cream, add to coffee, cocktails, pancakes, waffles, yogurt, or use as a filling for cupcakes. Warm gently for a thinner consistency if needed.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator in an airtight jar for up to 2 weeks. Warm before use, but avoid boiling to preserve flavor.
